newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay says orders three Airbus aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says orders three Airbus aircraft.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Thursday it had ordered two A340-300 and one A330-300 aircraft from Airbus Industrie for delivery in the last quarter of 1998.

"With the opening of Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok in 1998, we will have the opportunity to expand our frequencies and add new routes, and these additional aircraft will enable us to do that," Cathay managing director David Turnbull said.
In a statement, Turnbull said Cathay had been pleased with the performance and cost effectiveness of its mixed fleet of A330s and A340s.
The Hong Kong-based airline currently operates five A340-300s and 10 A330-300s, with one more of each type due for delivery in the next two months.
An order for three A340-300s for delivery in the first half of 1998 was made in September last year.
Cathay also operates one leased A340-200, which will have left the fleet by March.
Cathay said it has options for nine A330s or A340s, and has seven Boeing Co 777-300 aircraft on order with options for another 10.
